references.text: Describes the same symptoms of skin disease: swelling (שְׂאֵת), rash, and white spots (בַהֶרֶת) that require examination by the priest.
The preceding verse introduces the context of a boil (שְּׁחִין) that has been healed, which verse 19 continues to describe.
Also mentions the boil (הַשְּׁחִין) and the priest's assessment of whether the condition has spread or is a scar.
Parallel description of white or reddish spots (לְבָנָה אֲדַמְדֶּמֶת) in connection with burns, similar symptoms to those seen with boils.
Summarizes the various types of skin diseases including swelling (שְׂאֵת), rash, and light spots (בַהֶרֶת) mentioned in chapter 13.
Describes boils (שְׁחִין) as one of Egypt's plagues, using the same Hebrew word found in Leviticus 13:19.
Mentions Egypt's boils (שְׁחִין) as a curse, the same type of disease described in Leviticus 13.
Job was struck with painful boils (בִּשְׁחִין), using the same Hebrew word as in Leviticus 13:19.
